[32570 Enterprise Architecture Practice | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject provides a foundation in enterprise architecture, focusing on architecting software-intensive systems at a large scale. You'll examine current trends and challenges, applying contemporary practices to team-based architecture projects. The subject emphasises the integration and alignment of various enterprise architecture layers to support business objectives effectively.

[32570 Enterprise Architecture Practice | Learning and teaching activities]
This is a research inspired and practical project-based subject. The teaching and learning approach is based on learning by doing collaborative work in small groups. Students are expected to attend the weekly lectures and workshops. Lectures will help students to understand the fundamental building blocks and concepts of the enterprise software systems architecture. The workshops will give students the opportunities to apply these building blocks and concepts to practical problems and also build a working relationship with other students in a collaborative learning environment. In the beginning of teaching session, students are organised into groups, where each group acts as a start-up company. Group size depends on the number of enrollments in the subject. Each teaching and learning week is organised into pre-class, in-class and post-class activities.

Pre-class
Students are required to do pre-class research and reading using material and articles available from UTS, industry and scholarly databases (e.g. Gartner, IEEE, Wiley, AIS eLibrary), and watch any relevant videos if available before coming into the weekly sessions. Pre-class work is necessary for students because it will enable them to effectively perform in the upcoming lecture and workshop activities.

Class
Weekly lecture and workshop sessions are facilitated by the teaching staff. Students are expected to attend all the sessions for this subject. Lecture material and workshop tasks are posted on UTS learning platform before each weekly session. Students work in small groups on workshop case study project exercises and their own team project. The workshop format enables the students to inquire, discuss and apply the enterprise software systems architecture knowledge to real world business problems and scenarios for deep learning. Students in groups present their work to other groups and teaching staff for feedback during the workshop. Industry experts are regularly invited to lectures and workshops, if available, to share their practical experience and insights about the enterprise software systems architecture practices. Students also get an opportunity to present their work to industry experts during their architecture project showcase, which is held in the end of teaching session. This is intended to enhance the employability of students in industry. Students also bring their work-in-progress architecture project artefacts in the workshop sessions to get early and continuous feedback from the teaching staff. This will enable the students to identify and correct any issues before formal submission and consequently improve their learning and performance in the subject.

Post-class
Students are expected to extend their learning beyond the lecture and workshop sessions, by doing additional research and reading outside the weekly sessions. Students need to work on group assignments and revise the contents from the previous workshop for the upcoming in-workshop activities.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32570 Enterprise Architecture Practice | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Describe the enterprise software systems architecture project stakeholders, concerns and constraints for the effective architecture discovery, implementation and governance. (B.1)
SLO2: Describe the contribution of enterprise software systems architecture and its alignment to organizational goals. (B.1)
SLO3: Apply enterprise software systems architecture analysis practices to identify the current, transition and future states of the architecture. (C.1)
SLO4: Develop enterprise software systems architecture and plan its implementation. (C.1)
SLO5: Describe enterprise software systems architecture and its application to technical and business problems. (D.1)
